candidate.title: An unbiased comparison of 14 epigenetic clocks in relation to 174 incident disease outcomes.
candidate.abstract: Epigenetic Clocks have been trained to predict chronological age, healthspan and lifespan. Such clocks are often analysed in relation to disease outcomes - typically using small datasets and a limited number of clocks. Here, we present a large-scale (n = 18,859), unbiased comparison of 14 widely used clocks as predictors of 174 incident disease outcomes and all-cause mortality over 10-years of follow up. Second- and third-generation clocks significantly outperform first-generation clocks, which have limited applications in disease settings. Of the 176 Bonferroni significant (P  1%. However, there is minimal evidence for interactions between the clocks and sex or smoking (ever/never) status. Second- and third-generation epigenetic clocks show promise for disease risk prediction, particularly in relation to respiratory and liver-based conditions.
candidate.authors: Mavrommatis C, Belsky DW, Ying K, Moqri M, Campbell A, Richmond A, Gladyshev VN, Chandra T, McCartney DL, Marioni RE.

panel.reason: 1.8万人14种表观时钟系统比较，数据公开
14种表观时钟大规模头对头比较，必读基准

extraction.method: 系统比较14种表观遗传时钟与174种疾病关联
extraction.data: Generation Scotland DNA甲基化队列，18,859人
extraction.scenario: 疾病风险预测与时钟临床效用评估
extraction.benchmark: 14种第一至第三代表观遗传时钟
extraction.results: 完全校正模型下13种时钟与57种疾病共176个Bonferroni显著关联；GrimAge v2和DunedinPACE各72个显著关联
extraction.limitations: 以欧洲裔为主，观察性设计，部分时钟与协变量信息重叠
extraction.summary: 研究对14种表观遗传时钟与174种新发疾病进行了无偏系统比较。基于Generation Scotland队列18,859人，采用Cox和逻辑回归分析10年疾病发生。结果显示第三代和第二代时钟（如GrimAge v2、DunedinPACE）疾病预测关联最强，第一代时钟关联较少。
